QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_18

question.text: Which stage of an investor's life cycle is most suitable for higher equity allocation?

answer.text: Distribution stage when regular income is needed
Accumulation stage when the investor is young with a long time horizon
Retirement stage when capital preservation is the priority
All stages should have equal equity allocation

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 81 and 162-163, the accumulation stage has a long horizon, growth should be the priority, and equity is a suitable asset class. Per page 65, young earners and young families with long-term goals can allocate a meaningful share to growth assets (the workbook references roughly 60-70% in growth assets in that context). The Trap: Distribution and retirement stages emphasize lower risk and income stability rather than equity-heavy allocation. Equity weights should not be the same across all life stages. Note: Allocations should de-risk gradually as the investor approaches distribution. Specific equity-weight ranges should be tied to the source-backed numbers on page 65 rather than higher figures that are not in the checked pages.
